rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, also attributed to al-Farra, al-Kalbi, and Abu al-Ahwas, takes nahr as facing the qibla.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس قال: استقبل القبلة بنحرك وقاله الفراء والكلبي وأبو الأحوص.

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: The verb and nahr evoke facing one another; homes are described as confronting each other.
rows.anchor: سمعت بعض العرب يقول: منازلنا تتناحر أي نتقابل، نحر هذا بنحر هذا أي قبالته.

rows.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: In prayer, nahr means standing upright opposite the mihrab, by analogy with houses facing one another.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الأعرابي: هو انتصاب الرجل في الصلاة بإزاء المحراب من قولهم

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: A report from Ata interprets the command as sitting upright between the prostrations until the chest is visible.
rows.anchor: وروي عن عطاء قال: أمره أن يستوي بين السجدتين جالسا حتى يبدو نحره.

rows.speaker: سليمان التيمي
rows.claim: Sulayman al-Taymi interprets it as raising the hands in supplication toward the throat.
rows.anchor: وقال سليمان التيمي: يعني وارفع يدك بالدعاء إلى نحرك.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An unnamed interpretation takes fa-salli to mean worship.
rows.anchor: وقيل: «فصل» معناه: واعبد. وقال محمد بن كعب القرظي:

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
rows.claim: Since some pray and sacrifice to others, the Prophet's prayer and sacrifice must belong only to God, who gave him al-Kawthar.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب القرظي: { إنآ أعطيناك الكوثر * فصل لربك وانحر } يقول

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says the command is to worship and sacrifice for the Lord who singled the Prophet out with abundant good or the river al-Kawthar; matching that gift with one Eid sacrifice alone seems inadequate.
rows.anchor: قال ابن العربي: «والذي عندي أنه أراد: اعبد ربك، وانحر له، فلا يكن عملك

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi questions al-Shafi'i's view that slaughter before prayer is valid, citing the verse's order and the Prophetic distinction between sacrifice and ordinary meat.
rows.anchor: قال ابن العربي: «ومن عجيب الأمر: أن الشافعي قال: إن من ضحى قبل الصلاة أجزأه،

rows.speaker: البراء بن عازب
rows.claim: The Prophet said the day's first act is prayer, followed by slaughter; slaughtering beforehand is merely food for one's family, not a rite.
rows.anchor: عن البراء بن عازب، قال:

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: A report attributed to Ali interprets the verse as placing the right hand over the left during prayer; al-Daraqutni transmitted it.
rows.anchor: روي عن علي عليه السلام «فصل لربك وانحر» قال: وضع اليمين على الشمال

rows.speaker: علماؤنا
rows.claim: One legal position forbids folding the hands in obligatory prayer as leaning and does not recommend it in voluntary prayer.
rows.anchor: الأول: لا توضع فريضة ولا نافلة لأن ذلك من باب الاعتماد.

rows.speaker: علماؤنا
rows.claim: A second position leaves the hands unfolded in obligatory prayer but allows folding in voluntary prayer as assistance.
rows.anchor: الثاني: لا يفعلها في الفريضة، ويفعلها في النافلة استعانة

rows.speaker: ابن المنذر
rows.claim: A third position permits folding in both obligatory and voluntary prayers; Ibn al-Mundhir attributes it to Malik, Ahmad, Ishaq, and reportedly al-Shafi'i, while the rationalist jurists recommended it.
rows.anchor: الثالث: يفعلها في الفريضة والنافلة. وهو الصحيح لأنه ثبت أن رسول الله

rows.speaker: جماعة
rows.claim: Some authorities preferred letting the arms hang; reports name Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hasan al-Basri, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, and Malik, while Ibn Abd al-Barr treats both postures as Sunnah.
rows.anchor: ورأت جماعة إرسال اليد. وممن روينا ذلك عنه ابن المنذر والحسن

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: A report places the folded hands on the chest.
rows.anchor: فروي عن علي بن أبي طالب: أنه وضعهما على صدره.

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير، أحمد بن حنبل
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Ahmad place the hands above the navel; Ahmad sees no objection to placing them below it.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير وأحمد بن حنبل: فوق السرة. وقال: لا بأس

rows.speaker: طائفة
rows.claim: Another group places the hands below the navel; reports include Ali, Abu Hurayra, al-Nakha'i, and Abu Majliz, and the view is held by al-Thawri and Ishaq.
rows.anchor: وقالت طائفة: توضع تحت السرة. وروي ذلك عن علي وأبي هريرة

rows.speaker: الدارقطني
rows.claim: Al-Daraqutni transmits Anas's report that the Prophet raised his hands at the opening, bowing, rising from bowing, and prostration; its grading is discussed in the next segment.
rows.anchor: فاختلف في ذلك فروى الدارقطني من حديث حميد عن أنس قال: كان

rows.speaker: الدارقطني
rows.claim: Al-Daraqutni says only Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi raised the report from Humayd to the Prophet; the sound attribution is Anas's own practice.
rows.anchor: لم يروه عن حميد مرفوعا إلا عبد الوهاب الثقفي. والصواب: من فعل أنس.

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: In the two Ṣaḥīḥ collections, Ibn Umar reports raising the hands to shoulder level at prayer's opening, at bowing, and on rising from bowing, but not after prostration.
rows.anchor: وفي الصحيحين من حديث ابن عمر، قال: رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن المنذر
rows.claim: The practice of raising hands at opening, bowing, and rising is attributed to al-Layth, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad, Ishaq, Abu Thawr, and through Ibn Wahb to Malik.
rows.anchor: قال ابن المنذر: وهذا قول الليث بن سعد، والشافعي وأحمد وإسحاق وأبي ثور.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi endorses raising the hands at the established points because this is reliably transmitted from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وبه أقول لأن الثابت عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: سفيان الثوري وأصحاب الرأي
rows.claim: Another school raises the hands only at the opening takbir; al-Qurtubi calls this the well-known Maliki position and cites a report from Ibn Masud.
rows.anchor: وقالت طائفة: يرفع المصلي يديه حين يفتتح الصلاة، ولا يرفع فيما سوى ذلك.

rows.speaker: الدارقطني
rows.claim: The Ibn Masud report used for raising hands only at the opening is weak through Muhammad ibn Jabir; its sound form from Ibrahim is mursal and reports Abdullah's own practice, not the Prophet's.
rows.anchor: قال الدارقطني: تفرد به محمد بن جابر وكان ضعيفا عن حماد عن إبراهيم.

rows.speaker: الدارقطني
rows.claim: The report from al-Bara that the Prophet raised hands only at the opening is unreliable because the phrase that he did not repeat it was prompted to Yazid after he became confused.
rows.anchor: قال الدارقطني: وإنما لقن يزيد في آخر عمره: «ثم لم يعد» فتلقنه

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik's transmitted positions include never raising the hands during prayer; Ibn al-Qasim says he did not see Malik raise them at the opening and preferred leaving them down there.
rows.anchor: وفي مختصر ما ليس في المختصر عن مالك: لا يرفع اليدين في شيء من الصلاة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hater is identified as al-As ibn Wa'il; Arabs called a man abtar when his sons died and only daughters remained.
rows.anchor: أي مبغضك وهو العاص بن وائل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says al-As called the Prophet abtar after speaking with him, following the death of the Prophet's son Abdullah; the verse declares al-As cut off from good in both worlds.
rows.anchor: فيقال: إن العاص وقف مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يكلمه،

rows.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ikrima reports Ibn Abbas's account that Abu Jahl called Muhammad cut off after Ibrahim died; the verse identifies Abu Jahl as the truly cut-off one.
rows.anchor: وذكر عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال: كان أهل الجاهلية إذا مات ابن الرجل

rows.speaker: شمر بن عطية
rows.claim: Shammar ibn Atiyya identifies the hater as Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt.
rows.anchor: وقال شمر بن عطية: هو عقبة بن أبي معيط.

rows.speaker: السدي، ابن زيد
rows.claim: Al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd say Quraysh called Muhammad cut off after both al-Qasim and Ibrahim died, leaving no male heir to carry on his affairs.
rows.anchor: قالوا: بتر محمد، فليس له من يقوم بأمره من بعده فنزلت هذه الآية قاله السدي وابن زيد.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، عكرمة
rows.claim: Another account connects the verse to Quraysh's boast to Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf that they were better than the Prophet; 4:51 concerns Ka'b and this verse Quraysh.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه جواب لقريش حين قالوا لكعب بن الأشرف لما قدم مكة: نحن أصحاب السقاية

rows.speaker: عكرمة، شهر بن حوشب
rows.claim: Ikrima and Shahr ibn Hawshab say Quraysh described Muhammad as cut off from them for opposing them, and God announced that they were the ones cut off.
rows.anchor: قاله أيضا عكرمة وشهر بن حوشب.

rows.speaker: أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Linguistically, abtar is a man without children or an animal without a tail; more broadly it is anything whose trace of good has been severed.
rows.anchor: قال أهل اللغة: الأبتر من الرجال: الذي لا ولد له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term al-batīrāʾ appears in a report as a label for something truncated.
rows.anchor:
" ما هذه البتيراء "
وخطب زياد خطبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ziyad's sermon was called al-batrāʾ because he omitted praise of God and blessings on the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وخطب زياد خطبته البتراء لأنه لم يحمد الله فيها،

rows.speaker: ابن السكيت
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit calls the donkey and slave the two abtar beings because they bring little good.
rows.anchor: ابن السكيت: الأبتران: العير والعبد قال سميا أبترين لقلة خيرهما.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb means to make something cut off, while abāter describes a person who cuts ties with kin.
rows.anchor: ويقال: رجل أباتر بضم الهمزة: الذي يقطع رحمه.

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A cited poem uses abāter for a contemptible person who cuts off close kin.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: لئيم نزت في أنفه خنزوانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Batriyya are a Zaydi faction named after al-Mughira ibn Sa'd, nicknamed al-Abtar.
rows.anchor: والبترية: فرقة من الزيدية نسبوا إلى المغيرة بن سعد،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Ṣanbūr can mean an isolated palm whose base grows thin and peels.
rows.anchor: قيل: هو النخلة تبقى منفردة، ويدق أسفلها ويتقشر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Ṣanbūr can mean a solitary man without a child or brother.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو الرجل الفرد الذي لا ولد له ولا أخ.

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd records ṣanbūr as specifically the spout of a basin.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو مثعب الحوض خاصة حكاه أبو عبيد.

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A poetic line uses ṣanbūr in the phrase between a spout and the basin's rim.
rows.anchor: وأنشد: ما بين صنبور إلى الإزاء

rows.speaker: الجوهري
rows.claim: Al-Jawhari also records ṣanbūr as a metal pipe in a waterskin from which one drinks.
rows.anchor: والصنبور: قصبة تكون في الإداوة من حديد أو رصاص يشرب منها.

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq and others report from Ibn Abbas that four Quraysh leaders proposed mutual alternating worship and sharing whichever religion proved better; the sura answered them.
rows.anchor: ذكر ابن إسحاق وغيره عن ابن عباس:

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report says they offered belief if the Prophet would touch or worship some idols; Gabriel brought the sura, after which they despaired and harmed him and his companions.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو صالح عن ابن عباس: إنهم قالوا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article addresses a known group despite the generic wording: those already known to die in disbelief, a particular group expressed in general terms.
rows.anchor: والألف واللام ترجع إلى معنى المعهود وإن كانت للجنس من حيث إنها كانت صفة لأي

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi likewise says the sura answers particular people rather than all unbelievers, since some later believed and others died or were killed in disbelief.
rows.anchor: نزلت جوابا، وعنى بالكافرين قوما معينين، لا جميع الكافرين

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari rejects the altered reading 'say to those who disbelieved': it is a forgery that weakens the sura and erases God's deliberately humiliating direct address to the idolaters.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن الأنباري: وقرأ من طعن في القرآن: قل للذين كفروا

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن الأنباري
rows.claim: The canonical wording already entails 'say to the disbelievers' while adding the more forceful direct call, which the idolaters resented but could not harm the protected Prophet for using.
rows.anchor: فمعنى قراءتنا: قل للذين كفروا: يا أيها الكافرون دليل صحة هذا:

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن الأنباري
rows.claim: Al-Anbari argues that refusing the revealed address removes a special distinction God granted the Prophet.
rows.anchor: فمن لم يقرأ { قل يأيها الكافرون } كما أنزلها الله، أسقط آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of the repeated clauses is emphasis that cuts off the negotiators' hopes, like repeating an oath.
rows.anchor: وأما وجه التكرار فقد قيل إنه للتأكيد في قطع أطماعهم كما تقول: والله لا أفعل كذا،

rows.speaker: أكثر أهل المعاني
rows.claim: Most rhetoricians say Arabic repeats words for emphasis and clarity; they cite repeated divine refrains and clauses in 55:45, 83:10, 78:4-5, and 94:5-6.
rows.anchor: قال أكثر أهل المعاني: نزل القرآن بلسان العرب، ومن مذاهبهم التكرار إرادة التأكيد

rows.speaker: أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Arab speech also repeats commands and names, with examples from a Prophetic report and several poetic lines.
rows.anchor: ومنه قوله عليه السلام في الحديث الصحيح:

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that each repetition answers one turn of the idolaters' proposed annual exchange of worship, rejecting the arrangement forever.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هذا على مطابقة قولهم: تعبد آلهتنا ونعبد إلهك،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports Quraysh offered wealth, marriage, and followers if Muhammad stopped insulting their idols, then proposed worshipping Lat and Uzza for a year in return for a year of his worship.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: قالت قريش للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: نحن نعطيك من المال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: On this account the repeated 'I do not worship what you worship' answers their repeated proposals made on different occasions.
rows.anchor: فكان التكرار في «لا أعبد ما تعبدون» لأن القوم كرروا عليه مقالهم مرة بعد مرة.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further explanation treats repetition as intensification of the rejection.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنما كرر بمعنى التغليظ.

rows.speaker: الأخفش والمبرد
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash and al-Mubarrad assign the first pair to present worship and the second pair to future worship, with the Prophet also rejecting their past objects of worship.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أي «لا أعبد» الساعة «ما تعبدون. ولا أنتم عابدون»

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation says the idolaters discarded idols when tired of them; the Prophet rejects their current and former idols while affirming his worship of God.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنهم كانوا يعبدون الأوثان، فإذا ملوا وثنا، وسئموا العبادة له،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One tense analysis takes verses 2-3 as future, verse 4 as denying the Prophet's worship of their past gods, and verse 5 as a verbal repetition with a different sense.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن قوله تعالى: { لا أعبد ما تعبدون * ولا أنتم عابدون مآ أعبد } في الاستقبال.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final clause departs from the expected 'what I worshipped' to 'what I worship' to show that the deity worshipped before remains the one he worships; past and future may switch in divine reports.
rows.anchor: فعدل عن لفظ عبدت إلى أعبد، إشعارا بأن ما عبد في الماضي هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording uses ma rather than man for symmetry with the idol-directed clause, since their objects are idols; ma can nevertheless refer to rational beings.
rows.anchor: وقال: «ما أعبد»، ولم يقل: من أعبد ليقابل به «ولا أنا عابد ما عبدتم»

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A grammatical interpretation makes ma a verbal noun: the Prophet rejects their idolatrous worship, and they fail to worship God as a monotheist does because they associate partners with Him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن معنى الآيات وتقديرها: قل يا أيها الكافرون لا أعبد الأصنام

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: On the same reading, both clauses deny worship in the manner of the other: their worship is shirk, whereas his worship is pure monotheism.
rows.anchor: فأنا لا أعبد ما عبدتم، أي مثل عبادتكم ف«ما» مصدرية.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The verse threatens separation and is like 28:55: if they are content with their religion, the believers are content with theirs; one view says it was abrogated by the sword verse.
rows.anchor: فيه معنى التهديد وهو كقوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One opinion says the whole sura is abrogated.
rows.anchor: وقيل: السورة كلها منسوخة. وقيل: ما نسخ منها شيء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another opinion says nothing is abrogated because the verse is a report.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ما نسخ منها شيء لأنها خبر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Din here can mean the recompense for your religion and mine; their religion is called a religion because they believe in and adhere to it.
rows.anchor: ومعنى «لكم دينكم» أي جزاء دينكم، ولي جزاء ديني.

rows.speaker: نافع، البزي، هشام، حفص
rows.claim: Nafi, al-Bazzi with variation, Hisham, and Hafs open the yāʾ in 'wa-liya dīn'.
rows.anchor: وفتح الياء من «ولي دين» نافع، والبزي عن ابن كثير باختلاف عنه،

rows.speaker: نصر بن عاصم، سلام، يعقوب
rows.claim: Nasr ibn Asim, Salam, and Yaqub retain the yāʾ in 'dīnī' in both pause and continuation, treating it as part of the noun.
rows.anchor: وأثبت الياء في «ديني» في الحالين نصر بن عاصم وسلام ويعقوب

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: Other readers omit the yāʾ, following the consonantal codex and eliding it after the kasra, as in 26:78 and 3:50.
rows.anchor: الباقون بغير ياء، مثل قوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasr means assistance; its root is illustrated by rain helping drought-stricken land grow, and by the related verb forms and a poem.
rows.anchor: النصر: العون مأخوذ من قولهم: قد نصر الغيث الأرض: إذا أعان

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari identifies the promised victory as the Prophet's victory over Quraysh.
rows.anchor: ثم قيل: المراد بهذا النصر نصر الرسول على قريش الطبري.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view understands the victory as triumph over the unbelievers who fought him, since victory ultimately belonged to him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نصره على من قاتله من الكفار فإن عاقبة النصر كانت له.

rows.speaker: الحسن، مجاهد
rows.claim: Hasan, Mujahid, and others identify the conquest as the conquest of Mecca.
rows.anchor: وأما الفتح فهو فتح مكة عن الحسن ومجاهد وغيرهما.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Sa'id ibn Jubayr say the conquest refers to cities and palaces.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير: هو فتح المدائن والقصور.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other interpretations take the conquest to mean all lands or the knowledge God opened to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقيل: فتح سائر البلاد. وقيل: ما فتحه عليه من العلوم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idha can mean 'already', since the sura came after the conquest, though it may also mean 'when it comes to you'.
rows.anchor: و«إذا» بمعنى قد أي قد جاء نصر الله لأن نزولها بعد الفتح.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people are Arabs and others entering God's religion in successive groups; after Mecca fell, Arabs thought no one could resist Muhammad, whose sanctuary God had protected from the elephant army.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { ورأيت الناس } أي العرب وغيرهم.

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says an umma in this context numbers forty men.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك: والأمة: أربعون رجلا.

rows.speaker: عكرمة ومقاتل
rows.claim: Ikrima and Muqatil identify the people as Yemenis: seven hundred believers arrived, serving as callers to prayer, reciters, and proclaimers of God's oneness, which delighted the Prophet and moved Umar and Ibn Abbas to tears.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة ومقاتل: أراد بالناس أهل اليمن.

rows.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ikrima transmits Ibn Abbas's report that tender-hearted, gentle, generous Yemenis came and entered God's religion in groups.
rows.anchor: وروى عكرمة عن ابن عباس: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ: { إذا جآء نصر الله والفتح }

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: In Muslim, the Prophet describes Yemenis as tender-hearted and soft-hearted, with understanding and wisdom associated with Yemen.
rows.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Lord's relief comes from Yemen; interpretations are the relief of successive conversions or God's easing the Prophet's distress through the Yemenis, the Helpers.
rows.anchor:
وروي أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:
" إني لأجد نفس ربكم من قبل اليمن "

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jabir reports the Prophet saying people entered Islam in groups and will leave it in groups; al-Mawardi mentions the report and al-Tha'labi gives a neighbor-of-Jabir version.
rows.anchor: وروى جابر بن عبد الله قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means that after praying one should increase in glorification, praise, and seeking forgiveness.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { فسبح بحمد ربك واستغفره } أي إذا صليت فأكثر من ذلك.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets tasbih as prayer; praise thanks God for the victory and conquest, and istighfar asks for pardon.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معنى سبح: صل عن ابن عباس. «بحمد ربك» أي حامدا له على ما آتاك من الظفر والفتح.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes tasbih as declaring God free of imperfection while thanking Him, with persistent remembrance accompanying the request for forgiveness.
rows.anchor: وقيل: «فسبح» المراد به: التنزيه أي نزهه عما لا يجوز عليه مع شكرك له.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi says the prayer-and-increased-worship interpretation is the more evident one.
rows.anchor: «واستغفره» أي سل الله الغفران مع مداومة الذكر. والأول أظهر.

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports in Bukhari that after this sura was revealed the Prophet said in each prayer: glory and praise to God, and asked Him for forgiveness.
rows.anchor: روى الأئمة واللفظ للبخاري عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت:

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha also says he often said the same glorification and plea for forgiveness in bowing and prostration, interpreting the Qur'an through the practice.
rows.anchor:
وعنها قالت:
" كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يكثر أن يقول في ركوعه وسجوده:

rows.speaker: أم سلمة
rows.claim: A report outside the Ṣaḥīḥ collections says that near the end of his life the Prophet continually glorified God, sought forgiveness, and repented, explaining that he had been commanded to do so.
rows.anchor: وفي غير الصحيح: وقالت أم سلمة: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم آخر أمره

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that after the sura descended the Prophet strove until his feet swelled, his body thinned, he smiled less, and he wept more.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو هريرة: اجتهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد نزولها، حتى تورمت قدماه

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says the Prophet was never more earnest about the afterlife than when this sura was revealed.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: لم يكن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قط أشد اجتهادا

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says the Prophet recited the sura to Abu Bakr, Umar, and Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas; they rejoiced, but Abbas understood it as announcing the Prophet's death, which he affirmed.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: " لما نزلت قرأها النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على أصحابه، ومنهم أبو بكر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account places its revelation at Mina after the days of tashriq during the Farewell Pilgrimage; Umar and Abbas wept because they understood it as announcing the Prophet's death.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في منى بعد أيام التشريق، في حجة الوداع، فبكى عمر والعباس

rows.speaker: عمر، ابن عباس
rows.claim: Umar's Badr veterans interpret the sura as a command to seek forgiveness after victory, while Ibn Abbas reads it as notice that the Prophet's appointed time is near; Umar affirms this interpretation.
rows.anchor: وفي البخاري وغيره عن ابن عباس قال: كان عمر بن الخطاب يأذن لأهل بدر

rows.speaker: الترمذي
rows.claim: In al-Tirmidhi's version, Ibn Abbas identifies the verse as foretelling the Prophet's death and Umar says he knows no more than Ibn Abbas; al-Tirmidhi grades the report hasan sahih.
rows.anchor: ورواه الترمذي، قال: كان عمر يسألني مع أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's plea for forgiveness includes errors, ignorance, excess, mistakes, deliberate acts, joking, earlier and later acts, and what is public or hidden.
rows.anchor: قيل له: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول في دعائه: " رب اغفر لي خطيئتي وجهلي، وإسرافي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He considered himself inadequate before God's abundant gifts and regarded falling short of their due as a fault.
rows.anchor: فكان صلى الله عليه وسلم يستقصر نفسه لعظم ما أنعم الله به عليه،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One interpretation makes istighfar an appeal to remain attached to God in humble awareness of shortcomings, rather than relying on one's deeds.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون بمعنى: كن متعلقا به، سائلا راغبا، متضرعا على رؤية التقصير

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view treats seeking forgiveness as worship required for its own sake, not because forgiveness is needed.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الاستغفار تعبد يجب إتيانه، لا للمغفرة، بل تعبدا.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the command teaches the Prophet's community not to feel secure and abandon seeking forgiveness.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ذلك تنبيه لأمته، لكيلا يأمنوا ويتركوا الاستغفار.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes 'seek His forgiveness' to mean asking forgiveness for the Prophet's community.
rows.anchor: وقيل: «واستغفره» أي استغفر لأمتك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is ever accepting of those who glorify Him and seek forgiveness, turning toward them with mercy and accepting their repentance.
rows.anchor: { إنه كان توابا }: أي على المسبحين والمستغفرين، يتوب عليهم ويرحمهم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to an infallible Prophet to seek forgiveness underscores how much more everyone else needs it.
rows.anchor: وإذا كان عليه السلام وهو معصوم يؤمر بالاستغفار، فما الظن بغيره؟

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: In Muslim, Aisha says the Prophet increased his glorification and repentance because God told him he would see a sign among his community; he recognized that sign as the conquest and the people entering in groups.
rows.anchor: " كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يكثر من قول: «سبحان الله وبحمده، أستغفر الله

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar says the sura was revealed at Mina during the Farewell Pilgrimage; after it and 5:3 the Prophet lived eighty days, with later reports assigning spans after 4:176, 9:128, and 2:281.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عمر: نزلت هذه السورة بمنى في حجة الوداع، ثم نزلت

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil gives seven days as the Prophet's lifespan after the later revelation sequence; other chronological accounts were discussed under al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل سبعة أيام. وقيل غير هذا مما تقدم في «البقرة» بيانه،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In the two Ṣaḥīḥ collections, Ibn Abbas says the sura followed the Prophet's call from Mount Safa after 26:214: Quraysh affirmed he never lied, then Abu Lahab cursed him for warning them.
rows.anchor: في الصحيحين وغيرهما واللفظ لمسلم عن ابن عباس قال: لما نزلت

rows.speaker: الحميدي وغيره
rows.claim: An added report says Abu Lahab's wife came to the mosque carrying a stone, but God concealed the Prophet from her sight; she threatened him in verse, then left seeing only Abu Bakr.
rows.anchor: زاد الحميدي وغيره: فلما سمعت امرأته ما نزل في زوجها وفيها من القرآن،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh called the Prophet 'Mudhammam' to abuse him; he said God diverted their harm because they reviled Mudhammam while he was Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وكانت قريش إنما تسمي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مذمما، يسبونه، وكان يقول:

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
rows.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd gives another occasion: Abu Lahab asked what advantage he would receive by becoming Muslim, rejected equality with other Muslims, and the sura was revealed.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن سبب نزولها ما حكاه عبد الرحمن بن زيد

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن كيسان
rows.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Kaysan says Abu Lahab repeatedly turned visiting delegations away by calling the Prophet a liar and sorcerer; when one delegation insisted, he cursed the Prophet, who grieved and received the sura.
rows.anchor: وقول ثالث حكاه عبد الرحمن بن كيسان قال: كان إذا وفد على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account says Abu Lahab tried to stone the Prophet, God prevented him, and the verse announced that prevention.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن أبا لهب أراد أن يرمي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بحجر، فمنعه الله من ذلك،

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada interprets tabbat as 'lost'.
rows.anchor: ومعنى «تبت»: خسرت قاله قتادة.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، عطاء، ابن جبير، يمان بن رئاب
rows.claim: Other explanations gloss the verb as failed, strayed, perished, or became empty of every good.
rows.anchor: وقيل: خابت قال ابن عباس. وقيل: ضلت قاله عطاء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hands are singled out because most work is done with them: they lost, and Abu Lahab himself lost.
rows.anchor: وخص اليدين بالتباب، لأن العمل أكثر ما يكون بهما أي خسرتا وخسر هو.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, 'hands' stands for the whole person, as in 22:10, and Arabic uses a part for the whole; a poem illustrates the idiom.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المراد باليدين نفسه. وقد يعبر عن النفس باليد.

rows.speaker: الأصمعي عن أبي عمرو بن العلاء
rows.claim: Al-Asma'i reports that a caller after Uthman's killing recited a lament using tabban for the calamity of what people had done.
rows.anchor: حكى الأصمعي عن أبي عمرو بن العلاء أنه لما قتل عثمان رحمه الله سمع الناس هاتفا يقول:

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says the first tabbat is a curse and the second a factual report, as in 'May God destroy him; he has perished'; Ubay's and Abdullah's reading adds 'qad'.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: التب الأول: دعاء والثاني خبر، كما يقال: أهلكه الله وقد هلك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Lahab's personal name was Abd al-Uzza, and he was the Prophet's paternal uncle; his wife Umm Jamil was Abu Sufyan's sister, and both strongly opposed the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وأبو لهب اسمه عبد العزى، وهو ابن عبد المطلب عم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم.

rows.speaker: طارق بن عبد الله المحاربي
rows.claim: Tariq ibn Abdullah recounts seeing the Prophet preach the testimony of faith at Dhu al-Majaz while Abu Lahab followed him, bloodied his legs with stones, and called him a liar.
rows.anchor: قال طارق بن عبد الله المحاربي: إني بسوق ذي المجاز، إذ أنا بإنسان يقول:

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ata transmits Ibn Abbas's account that Abu Lahab accused Muhammad of magic, while marveling that Muhammad's food and drink satisfied people.
rows.anchor: وروى عطاء عن ابن عباس قال: قال أبو لهب: سحركم محمد!

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi rejects using this verse to prove that an unbeliever may receive a respectful kunya; he gives four reasons for God's use of Abu Lahab.
rows.anchor: وقد ظن قوم أن في هذا دليلا على تكنية المشرك وهو باطل،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The four reasons are that his given name invoked an idol, his kunya was better known, a kunya is lower than a proper name, and the name foreshadows his abode in Hell.
rows.anchor: الأول: أنه كان اسمه عبد العزى، والعزى: صنم،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account says his family called him Abu Lahab for his glowing, handsome face; God turned them from more favorable names such as Abu al-Nur toward the ill-omened fire-name.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل: اسمه كنيته. فكان أهله يسمونه أبا لهب،

rows.speaker: مجاهد، حميد، ابن كثير، ابن محيصن
rows.claim: These readers pronounce the hāʾ in 'Abi Lahab' with sukūn, while preserving it open in 'dhāt lahab' to fit the verse endings.
rows.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد وحميد وابن كثير وابن محيصن. «أبي لهب» بإسكان الهاء.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says that when God created the Pen He ordered it to record what would occur, including the doom of Abu Lahab.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لما خلق الله عز وجل القلم قال له: اكتب ما هو كائن

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says Abu Lahab could not escape the Fire, since his fate was written in the Preserved Book before he and his parents were created.
rows.anchor: وقال منصور: سئل الحسن عن قوله تعالى: { تبت يدآ أبي لهب }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Adam-and-Moses exchange is cited as a precedent for God's prior decree; the Prophet says Adam prevailed over Moses.
rows.anchor: ويؤيده قول موسى لآدم:أنت الذي خلقك الله بيده، ونفخ فيك من روحه

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: In the report from Abu Hurayra through Hammam, Adam asks how long before his creation God wrote the Torah; Moses answers two thousand years, including the statement that Adam disobeyed, so Adam asks why he is blamed for what was decreed.
rows.anchor: وفي حديث همام عن أبي هريرة أن آدم قال لموسى:

rows.speaker: طاوس، ابن هرمز، الأعرج عن أبي هريرة
rows.claim: A separate transmission gives forty years, rather than two thousand, for the interval before Adam's creation.
rows.anchor: وفي حديث طاووس وابن هرمز والأعرج عن أبي هريرة:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neither Abu Lahab's accumulated wealth nor the standing he earned could protect him from God's punishment.
rows.anchor: أي ما دفع عنه عذاب الله ما جمع من المال، ولا ما كسب من جاه.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains 'what he earned' as his children, since a man's child is among his earnings.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: من الولد وولد الرجل من كسبه.

rows.speaker: الأعمش عن ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Al-A'mash reads 'wa-ma iktasab' and transmits this reading from Ibn Masud.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش «وما اكتسب» ورواه عن ابن مسعود.

rows.speaker: أبو الطفيل
rows.claim: Abu al-Tufayl says Ibn Abbas called Abu Lahab's sons 'the vile earning' after they fought and shoved him while he tried to separate them.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو الطفيل: جاء بنو أبي لهب يختصمون عند ابن عباس، فاقتتلوا،

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports the Prophet saying the best food a man eats is from his own earnings and that his child is among his earnings.
rows.anchor: وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Abu Lahab offered to ransom himself with wealth and children if his nephew's warning proved true; the verse answered him.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: لما أنذر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عشيرته بالنار،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first ma may be a negation or a rhetorical question asking what his property gained him.
rows.anchor: و«ما» في قوله: { مآ أغنى }: يجوز أن تكون نفيا، ويجوز أن تكون استفهاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second ma may mean 'that which he acquired' or function with the verb as a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: و«ما» الثانية: يجوز أن تكون بمعنى الذي، ويجوز أن تكون مع الفعل مصدرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire is one of blazing, flaming intensity, a meaning discussed earlier in al-Mursalat.
rows.anchor: أي ذات اشتعال وتلهب. وقد مضى في سورة «المرسلات» القول فيه.

rows.speaker: القراء
rows.claim: The common reading has an open yāʾ, meaning he will enter the fire himself; other transmitted forms put the yāʾ in the passive, or double the lām to mean God will make him enter.
rows.anchor: وقراءة العامة: «سيصلى» بفتح الياء. وقرأ أبو رجاء والأعمش: بضم الياء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading is preferred because readers agree on it; the alternative readings likewise mean being made to enter the Fire.
rows.anchor: والأولى هي الاختيار لإجماع الناس عليها وهي من قوله: إلا من هو صال الجحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wife is Umm Jamil; Ibn al-Arabi instead calls her Umm Qabih and says she was cross-eyed.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { وامرأته } أم جميل.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، قتادة، السدي
rows.claim: They explain 'carrier of firewood' as carrying malicious gossip, since Arabs say someone gathers firewood against another for slander.
rows.anchor: { حمالة الحطب } قال ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة والسدي: كانت تمشي

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A poem glosses 'carriers of firewood' as slanderers who do so in peace and anger.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: إن بني الأدرم حمالو الحطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the wood wet signals its smoke and thus an increase in the evil.
rows.anchor: وجعل الحطب رطبا ليدل على التدخين، الذي هو زيادة في الشر.

rows.speaker: أكثم بن صيفي
rows.claim: Aktham ibn Sayfi warned his sons that slander is a consuming fire and that a gossip accomplishes in an hour what a magician does in a month.
rows.anchor: وقال أكثم بن صيفي لبنيه: إياكم والنميمة! فإنها نار محرقة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's reports condemn slander and the two-faced person; one calls the two-faced the worst of people.
rows.anchor: وثبت عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: " لا يدخل الجنة نمام "

rows.speaker: كعب الأحبار
rows.claim: Ka'b al-Ahbar says God withheld rain from Moses and the Israelites because an unrepentant slanderer was among them; they all repented and rain came.
rows.anchor: وقال كعب الأحبار: أصاب بني إسرائيل قحط، فخرج بهم موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: الفضيل بن عياض
rows.claim: Al-Fudayl ibn Iyad counts backbiting, slander, and lying among acts that ruin good deeds, break the fast, and invalidate ablution; slander is agreed to be a major sin.
rows.anchor: والنميمة من الكبائر، لا خلاف في ذلك حتى قال الفضيل بن عياض:

rows.speaker: عطاء بن السائب عن الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Sha'bi explains that gossip can provoke bloodshed, theft, and grave disorder, answering why it is paired with murder and usury in a reported hadith.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء بن السائب: ذكرت للشعبي قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: قتادة وغيره
rows.claim: Qatada and others say she mocked the Prophet's poverty, then was herself associated with carrying firewood because of stinginess despite her wealth.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة وغيره: كانت تعير رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالفقر.

rows.speaker: ابن زيد، الضحاك، ابن عباس
rows.claim: These authorities say she carried thorn branches and laid them in the Prophet's and his Companions' path at night; al-Rabi says he trod them like silk.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد والضحاك: كانت تحمل العضاه والشوك، فتطرحه بالليل على طريق النبي

rows.speaker: مرة الهمداني
rows.claim: Murra al-Hamdani recounts that an angel pulled a rock from under the exhausted Umm Jamil as she rested beneath her thorn bundle, killing her.
rows.anchor: فبينما هي حاملة ذات يوم حزمة أعيت، فقعدت على حجر لتستريح،

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr reads 'carrier of firewood' as carrier of sins, using the idiom of carrying one's burdens on one's back and citing 6:31.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: حمالة الخطايا والذنوب من قولهم: فلان يحتطب على ظهره

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The interpretation that she carries firewood in Hell is also mentioned, but judged far-fetched.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعنى حمالة الحطب في النار وفيه بعد.

rows.speaker: قراءة العامة
rows.claim: In the common nominative reading, 'hammālatu al-hatab' can be the wife's predicate; the clause about the rope can be a circumstantial phrase or a second predicate, or it can be an adjective with the rope-clause as predicate.
rows.anchor: وقراءة العامة «حمالة» بالرفع، على أن يكون خبرا «وامرأته» مبتدأ.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the wife is conjoined to the implicit subject of 'will burn', there is no pause at 'flame'; a pause may follow 'his wife', with 'carrier of firewood' as predicate of an omitted subject.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون «وامرأته» معطوفة على المضمر في «سيصلى» فلا يوقف

rows.speaker: عاصم
rows.claim: Asim reads the phrase in the accusative as blame or disparagement, making the description famous rather than restrictive, as in 33:61; Abu Qilaba reads 'hāmilata'.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عاصم «حمالة الحطب» بالنصب على الذم، كأنها اشتهرت بذلك،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jīd means the neck; Imru al-Qays's verse describes a graceful neck.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { في جيدها } أي عنقها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masad can be palm fiber, as in al-Nabigha's verse and another cited poem; it may also be camel hide or camel hair.
rows.anchor: وقال امرؤ القيس: وجيد كجيد الريم ليس بفاحش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural of jīd is ajyād and the plural of masad is amsād.
rows.anchor: { حبل من مسد } أي من ليف قال النابغة:

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda defines masad as a rope made of wool.
rows.anchor: وجمع الجيد أجياد، والمسد أمساد. أبو عبيدة: هو حبل يكون من صوف.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says masad is a rope made by twisting fibers from a tree that grows in Yemen.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: هي حبال من شجر تنبت باليمن

rows.speaker: الضحاك وغيره
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak and others say the rope refers first to this life: she taunted the Prophet's poverty while carrying wood in a palm-fiber neck rope that strangled her, and in the afterlife it is a rope of fire.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك وغيره: هذا في الدنيا فكانت تعير النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالفقر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، عروة بن الزبير
rows.claim: They interpret the rope as a chain seventy cubits long, entering her mouth, passing through her body, and looping around her neck.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في رواية أبي صالح: { في جيدها حبل من مسد } قال: سلسلة ذرعها

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the rope is a necklace of shells; Hasan also says she had shell beads around her neck.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة. «حبل من مسد» قال: قلادة من ودع.

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib says she had a valuable jewel necklace and swore by Lat and Uzza to spend it on hostility to Muhammad; it will become punishment around her neck.
rows.anchor: سعيد بن المسيب: كانت لها قلادة فاخرة من جوهر، فقالت: واللات والعزى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes the neck-rope a sign that she was barred from faith by prior wretchedness.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن ذلك إشارة إلى الخذلان يعني أنها مربوطة عن الإيمان بما سبق لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masad fundamentally means twisted fiber; the verb masada means to twist a rope firmly, and the word extends to tightly muscled bodies and related descriptions.
rows.anchor: والمسد: الفتل. يقال: مسد حبله يمسده مسدا أي أجاد فتله.

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says the disputed camel-hair poem has an inverted construction: 'zāhiq' is raised as the predicate of 'their marrow', not an adjective modifying weak.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: هو مرفوع والشعر مكفأ. يقول: بل مخهن مكتنز

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another grammarian interprets zāhiq as 'gone', with the phrase returning to describe the camels' weak marrow.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره: الزاهق هنا: بمعنى الذاهب كأنه قال: ولا ضعاف مخهن،

rows.speaker: الجوهري
rows.claim: Al-Jawhari records related words for strongly built men and women and musād for a container or skin holding clarified butter or honey.
rows.anchor: والمساد، على فعال: لغة في المساب، وهي نحى السمن، وسقاء العسل. قال جميعه الجوهري.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the rope is the one she used for wood, its survival in the Fire is no difficulty because God can renew it each time it burns.
rows.anchor: وأجيب عنه بأن الله عز وجل قادر على تجديده كلما احترق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their being consigned to Hell was conditional on dying in disbelief; since both died that way, the prediction came true and proves the Prophet's miracle.
rows.anchor: والحكم ببقاء أبي لهب وامرأته في النار مشروط ببقائهما على الكفر إلى الموافاة

rows.speaker: أبو رافع
rows.claim: Abu Rafi recounts that after Badr Abu Lahab struck him for identifying the white riders as angels; Umm al-Fadl hit Abu Lahab with a tent post, and he later died of a painful skin disease.
rows.anchor: قال أبو رافع: وكنت غلاما للعباس أنحت الأقداح في صفة زمزم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Lahab died seven nights after Badr; fear of contagion kept his body unburied for three days, and his sons finally covered it with stones from a distance.
rows.anchor: ورماه الله بالعدسة، فمات، وأقام ثلاثة أيام لم يدفن حتى أنتن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the one, unique without likeness, equal, spouse, child, or partner; aḥad derives from waḥid by changing initial wāw to hamza.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { قل هو الله أحد } أي الواحد الوتر، الذي لا شبيه له، ولا نظير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word aḥad is nominative as the predicate of huwa; alternatives make the clause 'the matter is that God is one' or treat aḥad as apposition to Allah.
rows.anchor: و { أحد } مرفوع، على معنى: هو أحد. وقيل: المعنى: قل: الأمر والشأن: الله أحد.

rows.speaker: جماعة
rows.claim: Some readers omit tanwin in 'aḥad Allah' for ease and to avoid two adjacent sukūns; a poem provides a parallel.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جماعة «أحد الله» بلا تنوين، طلبا للخفة،

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak transmits Ibn Abbas's gloss of al-Samad as the one to whom people turn with their needs; 16:53 is offered as a parallel.
rows.anchor: كذا روى الضحاك عن ابن عباس، قال: الذي يصمد إليه في الحاجات

rows.speaker: أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Lexicographers define al-Samad as the master to whom people turn in calamities and needs; a poem calls Amr ibn Masud this master.
rows.anchor: قال أهل اللغة: الصمد: السيد الذي يصمد إليه في النوازل والحوائج.

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Another view defines al-Samad as the enduring one who always was and always will be.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: الصمد: الدائم الباقي، الذي لم يزل ولا يزال.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation says al-Samad is explained by the following clauses, 'He neither begets nor is born'.
rows.anchor: وقيل: تفسيره ما بعده { لم يلد ولم يولد }.

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubay ibn Ka'b defines al-Samad as neither begetting nor being born, since every born thing dies and every dead thing is inherited.
rows.anchor: قال أبي بن كعب: الصمد: الذي لا يلد ولا يولد لأنه ليس شيء إلا سيموت،

rows.speaker: علي، ابن عباس، أبو وائل، سفيان
rows.claim: Ali, Ibn Abbas, Abu Wa'il, and Sufyan define al-Samad as the master whose mastery and honor are complete; a poem uses the phrase al-sayyid al-samad.
rows.anchor: وقال علي وابن عباس أيضا وأبو وائل شقيق بن سلمة وسفيان: الصمد: هو السيد

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra says God is independent of everyone while everyone needs Him.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو هريرة: إنه المستغني عن كل أحد، والمحتاج إليه كل أحد.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says al-Samad is the one sought for desired things and relied upon in calamities.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: إنه: المقصود في الرغائب، والمستعان به في المصائب.

rows.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
rows.claim: Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl defines al-Samad as the one who does what He wills and rules as He wants.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسين بن الفضل: إنه الذي يفعل ما يشاء ويحكم ما يريد.

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says al-Samad is complete and without flaw; al-Zibriqan's poem supplies the expression.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: إنه: الكامل الذي لا عيب فيه ومنه قول الزبرقان:

rows.speaker: الحسن، عكرمة، الضحاك، ابن جبير
rows.claim: Hasan, Ikrima, al-Dahhak, and Ibn Jubayr say al-Samad is solid and compact, with no hollow; they cite a poem describing compact gear.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن وعكرمة والضحاك وابن جبير: الصمد: المصمت الذي لا جوف له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi says the soundest definition is the first, supported by the word's derivation, and attributes it to al-Khattabi.
rows.anchor: قلت: قد أتينا على هذه الأقوال مبينة في الصمد، في كتاب الأسنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi condemns a Quran-denier who recited 'Allah al-Wahid al-Samad', omitted 'qul huwa', and changed aḥad; removing huwa destroys the answer's point.
rows.anchor: وقد أسقط من هذه السورة من أبعده الله وأخزاه، وجعل النار مقامه ومثواه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura answered polytheists who asked whether their Lord was gold, copper, or brass; huwa signals the answer, so omitting it falsifies the revelation.
rows.anchor: فأبطل معنى الآية لأن أهل التفسير قالوا: نزلت الآية جوابا لأهل الشرك لما قالوا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: صف لنا ربك،

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi transmits Ubay ibn Ka'b's report that polytheists asked the Prophet to describe or identify his Lord, prompting this sura.
rows.anchor: وروى الترمذي عن أبي بن كعب: أن المشركين قالوا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: The report glosses al-Samad as neither begetting nor being born, because God neither dies nor is inherited, and glosses kufuwan as having no likeness or equal.
rows.anchor: والصمد: الذي لم يلد ولم يولد لأنه ليس شيء يولد إلا سيموت،

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliya gives a similar report: when the Prophet mentioned their idols and they asked about his Lord, Gabriel brought the sura; al-Tirmidhi says this version is sounder.
rows.anchor: وروي عن أبي العالية: إن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ذكر آلهتهم فقالوا: انسب لنا ربك.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says 'He did not beget' rejects claims likening God to Mary, while 'was not begotten' rejects claims that Jesus or Ezra was God's child.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: { لم يلد } كما ولدت مريم، ولم يولد كما ولد عيسى وعزير.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These clauses refute Christians and those who claim Ezra is God's son.
rows.anchor: وهو رد على النصارى، وعلى من قال: عزير ابن الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kufuwan means anyone like Him; the syntax advances the predicate before the subject, maintaining the rhyme of the verse endings.
rows.anchor: { ولم يكن له كفوا أحد } أي لم يكن له مثلا أحد. وفيه تقديم وتأخير

rows.speaker: القراء
rows.claim: Readers vary between damma and sukūn on the fāʾ of kufuwan; both are eloquent dialect forms.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «كفوا» بضم الفاء وسكونها.

rows.speaker: حفص
rows.claim: Hafs reads kufuwan with a damma on fāʾ and without hamza; the forms are all eloquent.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حفص «كفوا» مضموم الفاء غير مهموز. وكلها لغات فصيحة.

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: In Bukhari, Abu Sa'id says a man repeatedly recited the sura; the Prophet swore that it equals one third of the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: ثبت في صحيح البخاري عن أبي سعيد الخدري:

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: In another report, the Prophet asks if anyone can recite a third of the Qur'an in one night and says 'Allah al-Wahid al-Samad' is that third.
rows.anchor:
وعنه قال:
" قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لأصحابه: «أيعجز أحدكم أن يقرأ ثلث القرآن في ليلة»

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet gathered people to recite a third of the Qur'an, read this sura, then clarified that it equals a third.
rows.anchor: وخرج عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Some scholars explain the equal-third merit by the unique divine names al-Samad and aḥad, which occur nowhere else in the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: قال بعض العلماء: إنها عدلت ثلث القرآن لأجل هذا الاسم،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation divides the Qur'an into rulings, promises and threats, and divine names and attributes; this sura contains the names-and-attributes third.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن القرآن أنزل أثلاثا، ثلثا منه أحكام، وثلثا منه وعد ووعيد،

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: Muslim's report from Abu al-Darda says God divided the Qur'an into three parts and made this sura one part; al-Qurtubi says this explains its title, Sura al-Ikhlas.
rows.anchor: ودل على هذا التأويل ما في صحيح مسلم، من حديث أبي الدرداء عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم،

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports that a commander on an expedition ended each prayer recitation with this sura because he loved it as the attribute of the Merciful; the Prophet said God loved him.
rows.anchor: الثانية: روى مسلم عن عائشة:

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas reports that an imam at Quba began every recitation with this sura, then added another sura in every rak'a; when challenged, he said he loved it and the Prophet promised that love would admit him to Paradise.
rows.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك قال: كان رجل من الأنصار يؤمهم في

rows.speaker: الترمذي
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi grades the Quba imam report hasan, gharib, sahih.
rows.anchor: قال: حديث حسن غريب صحيح.

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi takes the report as proof that the same sura may be repeated in every rak'a and describes an imam who used al-Fatiha and al-Ikhlas for each Tarawih rak'a, for ease and its merit.
rows.anchor: قال ابن العربي: «فكان هذا دليلا على أنه يجوز تكرار سورة في كل ركعة.

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says completing the Qur'an in Ramadan is not Sunnah; al-Qurtubi identifies this explicitly as Malik's position about mosque recitations.
rows.anchor: قلت: هذا نص قول مالك، قال مالك: وليس ختم القرآن في المساجد بسنة.

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi reports Anas saying the Prophet heard a man recite the sura and said Paradise was due to him; the report is graded hasan sahih.
rows.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك قال: أقبلت مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فسمع رجلا

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: A further report from Anas says daily recitation of the sura two hundred times erases fifty years of sins, except for an outstanding debt.
rows.anchor: عن ثابت البناني عن أنس بن مالك عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:
